newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope urges clemency for U.S. death row prisoner.
newsitem.headline: Pope urges clemency for U.S. death row prisoner.

text.p: Pope John Paul has made a personal appeal to the United States to spare a death row inmate who says he has new evidence that proves his innocence, the Vatican said on Friday.

It said the leader of the world's Roman Catholics had asked his nuncio (ambassador) in Washington to "intercede in his name to obtain clemency" for Joseph O'Dell, 55, who is scheduled to die by lethal injection in the state of Virginia next Wednesday.
O'Dell was convicted in 1985 of murdering 44-year-old secretary Helen Schartner and sentenced to death.

Virginia Governor George Allen on Thursday held a clemency hearing for O'Dell, who is asking the U.S. Supreme Court to review new DNA evidence he says proves that blood found on his shirt did not match the victim's.
Death penalty opponents say a court of appeals refused to admit the evidence and review the case because a submission deadline had expired.

The Vatican's statement on Friday followed an editorial in its newspaper L'Osservatore Romano this week which was critical of the O'Dell conviction and a protest by human rights groups on Thursday outside the U.S. embassy in Rome.
